nodes.rationale: Half of the ground plane is given a lower friction coefficient so the same vehicle model can be driven across a friction discontinuity, demonstrating per-contact-zone material assignment.

nodes.label: Collision Families
nodes.rationale: Grouping collidables into families suppresses unnecessary contacts, for example between adjacent track shoes.

nodes.label: demo_MCORE_particlesNSC
nodes.rationale: Container of homogeneous spherical particles carrying only 3 degrees of freedom each, dropping rotations to cut cost.

nodes.label: Chrono POSTPROCESS Module
nodes.rationale: Module that emits scripts and data files for external tools (POVray for rendering, GNUplot for graphs) instead of embedding a renderer or plotter, so heavy offline processing happens outside the simulation binary.

nodes.label: postprocess::ChGnuPlot
nodes.rationale: Generates the .gpl script from C++ and launches gnuplot automatically, sparing the user from writing the script, dumping a .dat file and invoking gnuplot by hand.

nodes.label: Embedded Data Plotting (no .dat file)
nodes.rationale: Data from ChVectorDynamic, ChFunction, ChFunctionInterp or ChMatrixDynamic columns is written inline into the .gpl file; the trade-off is that Replot does not work with embedded data.

nodes.label: postprocess::ChPovRay exporter
nodes.rationale: Writes .pov and .ini files during the run (ExportScript once, ExportData per timestep) so high-quality rendering happens later, offline.

nodes.label: ChParticleCloud with a sample shape asset
Visual Assets Shared Across Renderers
nodes.rationale: The same asset definitions drive VSG, Irrlicht and POV postprocessing, and are kept independent of the collision shapes.

nodes.label: Deep Reinforcement Learning with PyChrono
nodes.rationale: Training in a virtual physics environment instead of on real hardware cuts both the time and the risk of the operation, and DRL copes with unstructured, mutable environments where classical robotic control fails.

nodes.label: gym-chrono OpenAI Gym Environments
nodes.rationale: Offered as an open-source alternative to MuJoCo environments for users who want to leverage OpenAI Gym and Baselines.

nodes.label: Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)
nodes.rationale: On-policy actor-critic algorithm, so the code carries two networks: a Policy that maps state to action and a Value Function that scores the state.

nodes.label: ChronoPendulum Environment
nodes.rationale: Inverted pendulum balancing a pole on a cart: 1 action (force along z) and 4 observations.

nodes.label: ChronoAnt Environment
nodes.rationale: Four-legged walker learning to walk straight as fast as possible: 8 motor-torque actions and 30 observations.

nodes.label: Parallel Episode Collection (train_parallel.py)
nodes.rationale: Collecting data over multiple simulations with Python multiprocessing greatly speeds up late-stage training when episodes get long; checkpoints are interchangeable with serial training since the network architecture is identical.

nodes.label: Checkpoint Saving and Restoring (Policy, VF, scaler.dat)
PyChrono Tutorials Index
nodes.rationale: Demo sources must match the installed Chrono version: from src/demos/python/ when built from a clone, or from pychrono/demos/ in site-packages when installed from conda.

nodes.label: Watertight Mesh Requirement for Concave Collision
nodes.rationale: Concave-mesh collision is slower and less robust than primitives, so the recommended trade-off is a detailed mesh for visualization plus a few primitives for collision; when a mesh must collide it has to be watertight (no gaps, no repeated vertices).

nodes.label: C++-side Python Parsing
nodes.rationale: The PYTHON module is the mirror image of PyChrono: it lets a C++ program load and execute Python programs, rather than exposing Chrono to Python. Demos live under src/demos/pyparser.

nodes.label: Chrono::ROS Module
nodes.rationale: Exists to exchange information between Chrono datatypes and ROS messages so an external autonomy stack can drive/observe a Chrono simulation; exposed both in C++ and through PyChrono so Python-based autonomy stacks need no C++ build.

nodes.label: ChROSHandler Extension Point
nodes.rationale: Custom logic is added by extending the ChROSHandler base class with user publishers/subscribers rather than by modifying the bridge, keeping user code out of the transport layer.

nodes.label: Autonomy Research Testbed
nodes.rationale: SBEL (UW-Madison) effort using Chrono and Chrono::ROS as the development platform for autonomy stacks on a scale vehicle; cited as the complex end-to-end example beyond the shipped demos.

nodes.label: Chrono Sensor Models Library
nodes.rationale: Sensors are shipped as parameterized models (camera, lidar, radar, GPS, IMU, tachometer) plus a separate library of pre-defined concrete instances, so users can pick a stock device or parameterize their own.

nodes.label: demo_SEN_cornell_box
nodes.rationale: A Cornell box with several light types is used as the benchmark scene for observing color bleeding in the camera model.

nodes.label: Chrono::SolidWorks Add-In
nodes.rationale: SolidWorks is used as a preprocessor: the add-in exports an assembly to a .py Chrono system description so CAD authoring and simulation stay decoupled.

nodes.label: Pre-exported Model Tutorials
nodes.rationale: Ships ready-made exports so users can exercise the import path without first buying a SolidWorks license and installing the add-in.

nodes.label: Chrono::SolidWorks Add-in
nodes.rationale: Uses SolidWorks CAD as a preprocessor for Chrono: the CAD assembly already carries geometry, mass and inertia, so exporting it avoids hand-authoring a mechanism in code.

nodes.label: Mate-to-ChLink Export Mapping
nodes.rationale: Each moving SolidWorks part becomes a ChBody and each SolidWorks mating constraint becomes a ChLink; sub-assemblies must be switched from 'Solve as Rigid' to 'Solve as Flexible' or their internal joints are lost, and the first inserted part must be changed from Fixed to Floating so it can be constrained in Chrono instead.

nodes.label: Exported Chrono System (.py)
nodes.rationale: The exporter emits a Python module plus a <name>_shapes directory of .obj visualization meshes, separating simulation description from render geometry so meshes can be simplified in external tools such as Blender.

nodes.label: test.py / run_test.py Runner Stub
nodes.rationale: Auto-generated stub that loads the exported .py into a ChSystem, sets up Irrlicht or POV visualization and runs the loop; kept deliberately simple as a template the user is expected to copy and extend. Takes -f/--filename, -d/--timestep, -T/--Tlength, -v/--visualization, -p/--datapath.

nodes.label: POVray Postprocessing Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Batch alternative to the Irrlicht realtime view: Chrono postprocess emits .pov/.ini scripts, POVray raytraces .bmp frames into anim/, VirtualDub assembles them into an AVI (MPEG4/DivX suggested, 25-30 fps).

nodes.label: Four-Cylinder Engine Assembly
nodes.rationale: Built by replicating the piston_rod subassembly three more times while avoiding redundant constraints.

nodes.label: chrono.ImportSolidWorksSystem
nodes.rationale: Loads the exported model by module name without the .py suffix and requires an explicit './' prefix even in the current directory; returns exported items which the caller adds to a ChSystemNSC.

nodes.label: ChPythonEngine::ImportSolidWorksSystem (C++)
nodes.rationale: C++ cannot load the exported .py directly, so the PYTHON module must be linked and an embedded ChPythonEngine used to obtain the same effect.

nodes.label: Exported Coordinate Systems as ChMarker
nodes.rationale: Adding a named SolidWorks CoordinateSystem feature and fetching it via ChSystem::SearchMarker is smarter than typing a ChFramed by hand, because the CAD already knows the exact position and axis direction.

nodes.label: ChLinkMotorRotationSpeed Crank Motor
nodes.rationale: The exporter emits only mating constraints, never actuation, so a driving motor must be added in user code between the crankshaft and ground; the Z axis of the supplied frame is the rotation axis, SetSpindleConstraint picks the connection type and SetMotorFunction takes a ChFunction.

nodes.label: ChPovRayAssetCustom Material Override
nodes.rationale: Default rendered surfaces look like white chalk; attaching a custom POVray statement fragment as an asset on a body lets per-shape pigments/finishes be injected into the generated scripts without changing the exporter.

nodes.label: ChBodyAuxRef Reference Frame vs COG
nodes.rationale: Exported bodies are ChBodyAuxRef, not ChBody, because ChBody assumes the center of mass coincides with the body reference frame while a CAD part's origin generally does not; the COG is computed by SolidWorks from assigned material densities. For a rigid sub-assembly the reference frame is the sub-assembly origin.

nodes.label: ChCamera Attached to a Moving Body
Opt-in Collision Shape Assignment
nodes.rationale: SolidWorks parts generate no collision shapes by default so that only parts that need them pay the computational overhead, and because no automatic decomposition of generic concave shapes into Chrono primitives exists yet (a convex-decomposition tool is under development, but hand-placed convex shapes usually give better results). Shapes are authored as extra SolidWorks solid bodies with 'Merge results' unchecked and tagged via 'Set body as collision shape'; the tagged body must not be edited afterwards or it stops being recognized as a primitive.

nodes.label: Supported Convex Collision Primitives
nodes.rationale: Spheres, cylinders, boxes and convex hulls, plus groups of them; a single part may carry several primitives (e.g. box + cylinder to approximate a capital with a torus).

nodes.label: Zero-Density Air Material on Collision Shapes
nodes.rationale: The add-in assigns a zero-density material (Air) to a tagged collision body so SolidWorks does not double-count its mass when computing the part's inertia; the visible body keeps the real material. The shape is also recolored semi-transparent pink since it overlaps the detailed shape.

nodes.label: Collision Envelope and Margin Defaults
nodes.rationale: SetDefaultSuggestedEnvelope/Margin must be called before importing the model or creating the ChSystem, and matter most for very large or very small objects; with compliant materials the envelope should be set to zero.

nodes.label: ChContactMaterialNSC Compliance vs Restitution
nodes.rationale: Non-compliant NSC materials are perfectly inelastic. Elasticity can come either from compliance (requires smaller time steps and a zero collision envelope) or from a restitution coefficient, which is meaningless once compliance is enabled and is physically accurate only in very simple scenarios because it rests on the simple Newton restitution assumption.

nodes.label: Earthquake Shaker Link
nodes.rationale: The floor is freed from its CAD 'fixed' state and tied to the implicit 'ground' body by a ChLinkLockLock whose X motion law is the product of two ChFunctionSine harmonics; mate constraints in the assembly must be deactivated first or the building cannot fall.

nodes.label: SolidWorks Spider Robot Demo
nodes.rationale: Six-legged crawling robot whose motion is driven by 18 actuators, modeled in SolidWorks, exported to spider_robot.py and simulated from demo_SW_spider_robot.py via PyChrono.

nodes.label: SolidWorks Instance-Name Mangling
nodes.rationale: A part shown as Name<N> in the SolidWorks GUI is exported as Name-N on the Python side, so body lookups by name must use the hyphen form.

nodes.label: Time- and Space-coherent Distributed World
nodes.rationale: SynChrono synchronizes separately-simulated vehicles and robots into one coherent Chrono world, and ships out-of-the-box wrapping of Chrono::Vehicle models, Irrlicht and Sensor visualization, intelligent intersections, and SCM terrain.

nodes.label: MPI-based Synchronization
nodes.rationale: mpirun -n <nodes> initializes every node in one command, which is why MPI demos are the simplest to launch.

nodes.label: FastDDS-based Synchronization
nodes.rationale: DDS has no launcher equivalent to mpirun, so each node is started manually with -n <num nodes> -d <this node num>; in exchange nodes can be spread across physical machines via IP.

nodes.label: Runtime Command-line Configuration
nodes.rationale: All SynChrono demos expose their options as command-line arguments specifically so that changing a scenario does not require a recompile; --help enumerates them per demo.

nodes.label: chrono_types::make_shared
nodes.rationale: Many Chrono classes hold fixed-size vectorizable Eigen members and overload operator new to return 16-byte-aligned pointers. std::make_shared uses placement new and bypasses that overload, so Chrono ships replacement functions in the chrono_types namespace that fall back to std::make_shared when safe and otherwise allocate aligned memory. User code should always use chrono_types::make_shared; STL containers of such classes need Eigen::aligned_allocator.

nodes.label: Template-based Vehicle Framework
nodes.rationale: Wheeled and tracked vehicles are built from parameterized templates of vehicles and subsystems, so a concrete vehicle is a parameter set rather than new code; extension demos (articulated chassis, tractor-trailer) show subclassing the framework.

nodes.label: Pre-defined Vehicle Models Library
nodes.rationale: Ships HMMWV, Sedan, Citybus, UAZ, M-role, MAN (5t/7t/10t), Kraz, FMTV, Gator and RC wheeled models plus M113 and Marder tracked models as a separate library alongside the main VEHICLE library.

nodes.label: Granular Terrain with Moving Patch
nodes.rationale: Granular terrain demos run through the MULTICORE module, and the moving-patch feature limits the simulated granular region to the neighborhood of the vehicle.

nodes.label: JSON Vehicle Specification
nodes.rationale: Both wheeled and tracked vehicles can be defined entirely through JSON specification files, giving the same model as the compiled-in variant without writing code.

nodes.label: Vehicle Test Rigs (suspension, tire, track assembly)
nodes.rationale: Subsystems can be exercised in isolation on dedicated rigs rather than only inside a full vehicle.

nodes.label: Doxygen HTML Footer Template
nodes.rationale: Two alternative footers are emitted depending on GENERATE_TREEVIEW: a navpath breadcrumb when treeview is on, a bootstrap grid footer otherwise.

nodes.label: Project Chrono Attribution (UW-Madison / Parma)
nodes.rationale: Community project led by the University of Wisconsin-Madison and the University of Parma, open-source and hosted on GitHub.

nodes.label: Bootstrap Navigation Bar
nodes.rationale: The generated API docs reuse the projectchrono.org bootstrap navbar (jQuery + bootstrap CDN, doxy-boot.js, hover dropdowns) so Doxygen output visually matches the main website.

nodes.label: Versioned API Documentation Navigation
nodes.rationale: The Documentation dropdown pins one entry per published API version (development branch, 10.0.0, 9.0.0) alongside FAQ, PyChrono, validation studies and white papers.

nodes.label: Chrono src Build Root
nodes.rationale: Drives all module subdirectories in a deliberate order: Chrono::Mumps must be configured before any module that may depend on Intel MKL. Requires C++17 (detected per compiler family because CMake's standard flags cannot be trusted for PGI).

nodes.label: Eigen3 Discovery and Configuration
nodes.rationale: Tries Eigen 5.0 first, then 3.3; sets _ENABLE_EXTENDED_ALIGNED_STORAGE for MSVC 15.8+ and EIGEN_DONT_PARALLELIZE when Eigen OpenMP is off. Definitions land on the Eigen3::Eigen INTERFACE target so they reach every Chrono target.

nodes.label: AMD Eigen Alignment Clamp
nodes.rationale: Host-side Chrono classes hold fixed-size Eigen objects that AVX would require to be 32-byte aligned, but some allocation paths (demos, visualization, MBS coupling) do not guarantee that; in ROCm builds this aborted demo_FSI-SPH_CouetteFlow before any SPH kernel ran. Clamping EIGEN_MAX_ALIGN_BYTES/EIGEN_MAX_STATIC_ALIGN_BYTES to 16 keeps SSE-friendly vectorization without the fragile over-alignment. Deliberately keyed on CHRONO_GPU_VENDOR_RESOLVED == AMD rather than CHRONO_HIP_FOUND, because it changes the ABI of every target and must not fire on a CUDA build that merely has ROCm installed.

nodes.label: ROCm-packaged Thrust Exclusion
nodes.rationale: A Thrust that resolved inside the ROCm tree is dropped for host-side Chrono targets in HIP builds; keyed on the resolved vendor, not on CHRONO_HIP_FOUND, so an NVIDIA build with ROCm merely present keeps its Thrust.

nodes.label: Three-Layer GPU Backend Resolution
nodes.rationale: Layer 0 ChronoGPUVendor answers which hardware is targeted, layer 1 ChronoGPUToolchains which SDKs are usable, layer 2 ChronoGPUModule what each feature compiles as. ChronoGPUDetect must be include()d at file scope because it calls enable_language().

nodes.label: ChConfig.h Generation
nodes.rationale: Every enabled module and detected capability (SIMD, OpenMP, CUDA, HIP, Thrust, HDF5, YAML, gtest, gbenchmark) is turned into a #define/#undef substitution variable and configured into chrono/ChConfig.h, which is how C++ code discovers the build configuration.

nodes.label: yaml-cpp FetchContent Integration
nodes.rationale: Fetched from the in-tree third-party directory; sample tools are force-disabled because Chrono uses none of them and they escape the library-level warning suppression. MSVC warning pragmas are PUBLIC since yaml-cpp headers are reached through Chrono's own src/ include root where the SYSTEM include mechanism cannot mark them external. Disabled entirely on VS 2019 and older.

nodes.label: ChronoConfig.cmake Package Export
nodes.rationale: Two variants of the package config are generated, one for the build tree and one for the install tree, alongside ChronoTargets.cmake exported under the Chrono:: namespace.

nodes.label: Chrono_core Precompiled Header
nodes.rationale: Chrono_core has ~500 translation units that nearly all include the core linear-algebra headers plus STL streams/containers; Build Insights shows Eigen dominates template instantiation and ChMatrix.h is the single most-included header. ChMatrix.h is the PCH anchor rather than a bare Eigen include because it defines EIGEN_MATRIXBASE_PLUGIN/EIGEN_SPARSEMATRIX_PLUGIN first, reproducing Chrono's exact Eigen configuration, and transitively covers ChArchive.h/ChArchiveASCII.h. Scope is PRIVATE so consumers are not forced onto it; ChCorePCH.h is __cplusplus-guarded so C sources get an empty PCH.

nodes.label: Chrono_core Thrust Device System (OMP/CPP)
nodes.rationale: Chrono_core selects THRUST_DEVICE_SYSTEM_OMP when OpenMP is enabled and THRUST_DEVICE_SYSTEM_CPP otherwise, and keeps both definitions PRIVATE.

nodes.label: SYSTEM Include Split for Third-Party Headers
nodes.rationale: Include directories that resolve only third-party headers (bullet, chrono_thirdparty, HACDv2) are kept in a separate list so they can be marked SYSTEM; warnings raised inside those headers are then suppressed both in Chrono and in downstream projects.

nodes.label: Chrono_cascade Library Target
nodes.rationale: Off by default (CH_ENABLE_MODULE_CASCADE); links Chrono_core PRIVATE and the OCCT libraries PUBLIC, and self-disables by forcing the option back OFF if OpenCASCADE is not found. Platform defines WNT (Windows) and HAVE_IOSTREAM/HAVE_LIMITS_H (Unix) are what OpenCASCADE headers expect.

nodes.label: OCCT_LIBS Link List
nodes.rationale: An explicit hand-maintained list of OpenCASCADE toolkits (TKernel, TKMath, TKBRep, TKDESTEP, TKXCAF...) is linked PUBLIC instead of relying on an OpenCASCADE imported-target closure; the include directory is added SYSTEM to silence third-party warnings.

nodes.label: Optional Irrlicht Dependency of Cascade
nodes.rationale: ChCascadeIrrMeshTools is compiled into the module and Chrono_irrlicht is linked only when the IRRLICHT module is enabled; the choice is also published upward through DEPENDENCIES_CASCADE in PARENT_SCOPE.

nodes.label: Chrono_dem_vsg Visualization Target
nodes.rationale: Applies the GPU backend Chrono_dem actually resolved to, not merely 'a CUDA toolkit exists somewhere' - those are no longer the same statement.

nodes.label: Chrono::DEM Single-Source GPU Backend
nodes.rationale: Chrono::DEM is not dual-source: one set of .cu kernels compiles either as CUDA or as HIP, so PREFER CUDA means 'use the vendor-native SDK for these sources', not 'pick between two source trees'. Both HIP platforms are accepted because the kernels use hipCUB on ROCm and plain CUB when HIP targets NVIDIA. Requires Eigen >= 3.3.6.

nodes.label: FMU export capability (CH_ENABLE_FMU_EXPORT)
nodes.rationale: FMU export is force-disabled unless Chrono is built statically (BUILD_SHARED_LIBS off) and, on MSVC, with a statically-linked runtime (CH_USE_MSVC_STATIC_RUNTIME). An FMU must be a self-contained shared object, so any Chrono runtime dependency it would otherwise inherit from a shared build would not be resolvable inside the importing tool.

nodes.label: fmu-forge third-party distribution
nodes.rationale: Defaults to the src/chrono_thirdparty/fmu-forge submodule but is overridable via FMU_FORGE_DIR so users can point at their own fmu-forge tree; the whole directory is installed under include/chrono_thirdparty because the FMI import/export headers are header-only wrappers over it.

nodes.label: FMI2/FMI3 platform triple detection
nodes.rationale: FMI 2.0 and FMI 3.0 name the binary platform differently (win64 vs x86_64-windows), so the module derives both FMI2_PLATFORM and FMI3_PLATFORM from WIN32/APPLE/UNIX plus CMAKE_SIZEOF_VOID_P and exposes them as public compile definitions; when detection fails the values become user-editable cache entries instead of aborting the build.

nodes.label: Chrono_fsi Generic Interface Library
nodes.rationale: Deliberately dependency-free with respect to other Chrono modules (DEPENDENCIES_FSI is empty): it is the generic FSI interface that the SPH and TDPF fluid backends both implement.

nodes.label: Chrono_fsisph_vsg Visualization Target
nodes.rationale: Under HIP its visualization source is compiled with LANGUAGE HIP because it includes FSI data-manager headers referencing rocThrust/rocPRIM device types that do not compile as plain C++.

nodes.label: SPH Thrust Device-System Wiring
nodes.rationale: Thrust's device system follows the HIP PLATFORM, not merely the fact that the backend is HIP: THRUST_DEVICE_SYSTEM_HIP means rocThrust, which exists only in ROCm, so when HIP targets NVIDIA the correct system is CUDA. Computed once at submodule scope because Chrono_fsisph and the VSG plugin must agree, and letting the plugin decide separately is exactly how it went out of step. The definitions stay PRIVATE and nothing is exported: no installed header includes <thrust/...>, exporting THRUST_DEVICE_SYSTEM_CUDA collided with Chrono::Multicore's THRUST_DEVICE_SYSTEM_OMP (last one silently winning, macro-redefinition warnings on vehicle demos), and exporting _CPP would silently demote a consumer's own device Thrust - Chrono::Sensor calls thrust::device_vector on CUDA device pointers and would segfault at runtime rather than fail to build.

nodes.label: Asymmetric GPU Runtime Visibility
nodes.rationale: CUDA is PUBLIC because public headers switch on CHRONO_USE_CUDA and then include <cuda_runtime.h>, so consumers inheriting the definition must also inherit CUDA include directories from CUDA::cudart_static (a public definition with a private link breaks every downstream target, Chrono_parsers first). HIP is PRIVATE because public consumers are ordinary C++ TUs and the HIP target's definitions would force Thrust onto rocPRIM in code that never asked for it.

nodes.label: Splashsurf Surface Reconstruction
nodes.rationale: Optional external executable; when absent the surface reconstruction utility is compiled out via CHRONO_HAS_SPLASHSURF.

nodes.label: Chrono_fsitdpf Library Target
nodes.rationale: Requires Eigen >= 3.3.6 and HDF5 (used by the HydroChrono h5_reader); disables itself with a warning when either is missing.

nodes.label: HydroChrono Source Integration
nodes.rationale: HydroChrono wave/radiation/excitation/hydrostatics sources are compiled directly into Chrono_fsitdpf from a path (CH_HYDROCHRONO_DIR) that defaults to the third-party submodule but can be pointed at a different tree; their warnings are suppressed as external code.

nodes.label: Chrono_irrlicht library target
nodes.rationale: Re-exports IRRLICHT_INCLUDE_DIR/LIBRARY/DLL to PARENT_SCOPE and installs FindIrrlicht.cmake into both build and install trees so downstream ChronoConfig consumers can re-resolve Irrlicht.

nodes.label: Spectra eigenvalue solver dependency
nodes.rationale: Hard requirement for the modal module (generalized symmetric/unsymmetric eigenvalue solvers and Krylov-Schur). If not found the module emits editable spectra_INCLUDE_DIR / spectra_DIR cache entries and returns rather than failing the whole configure.

nodes.label: Chrono Models Build Config
nodes.rationale: Robot models build independently, but vehicle models are force-disabled in the cache when Chrono::Vehicle is off rather than merely defaulting off.

nodes.label: ChronoModels_robot library target
nodes.rationale: Bundles RoboSimian, Viper, Turtlebot, Curiosity, copters and industrial robot/kinematics models into one target; the URDF-driven RoboSimianURDF variant is only compiled when the parsers module has urdfdom (CH_USE_URDF).

nodes.label: ChronoModels_vehicle library target
nodes.rationale: One monolithic target containing every concrete vehicle (jeep, bmw, gclass, hmmwv, feda, mtv, mrole, uaz, unimog, duro, generic, sedan, citybus, gator, m113, marder, man, artcar, kraz). ANCF/Reissner deformable tires and band-ANCF track assemblies are conditionally added only when CH_ENABLE_MODULE_FEA is on.

nodes.label: Vehicle subsystem file-group decomposition
nodes.rationale: Each vehicle is split into the same recurring subsystem groups - chassis, suspension, steering, driveline, brake, powertrain (engine + transmission), tire, wheel - mirrored both in directory layout and in source_group names. This uniform template is what lets templated vehicle models be swapped subsystem-by-subsystem across otherwise unrelated vehicles.

nodes.label: BMW E90 vehicle model data sources
nodes.rationale: Vehicle parameters come from SAE 2007-01-0818 (NADS 2006 BMW 330i parameterization); missing powertrain data are filled from a public BMW datasheet and other internet sources.

nodes.label: Duro multipurpose transport vehicle model
nodes.rationale: Modeled to demonstrate the unusual Bucher/Mowag Duro suspension principle; almost all data are estimated from Wikipedia, enthusiast sites and drawings because no manufacturer dataset is public.

nodes.label: FED Alpha tactical vehicle model
nodes.rationale: Data from the Keweenaw Research Center public release; the 3D graphic representation is derived from the CAD files and tire files come from public sources.

nodes.label: Gator utility vehicle model
nodes.rationale: Based on a John Deere TE 4x2 E-Gator; parameters taken from manufacturer brochures and adjusted for payload modifications, with tire data estimated from OEM tire specs (22.5x10-8 front, 25x12-9 rear).

nodes.label: Mercedes G-class (G500) vehicle model
nodes.rationale: The real G-Class suspension uses elasto-kinematic elements; the Chrono model deliberately simplifies it to a pure kinematic design.

nodes.label: Kraz semi-trailer truck model
nodes.rationale: Longhaul model pairing a Krone dry-liner semi-trailer with a Kraz 64431 tractor; all data extracted from the two manufacturers' public brochures.

nodes.label: M113 tracked APC model data sources
nodes.rationale: Assembled from several public sources - Wallin/Shabana joint-formulation and chain-dynamics studies, Afonso's ride-dynamics thesis, Keays' track load/stress report, and a Tankograd reference volume - since no single authoritative parameter set exists.

nodes.label: MAN Kat 1 truck models
nodes.rationale: Chassis data from P. Ocker's MAN book, engine data from Deutz, tire data estimated from a Pacejka truck tire dataset.

nodes.label: mrole multi-role vehicle model
nodes.rationale: A simplified stand-in for the KMW/RLS 'Boxer'. Engine, drivetrain and suspension approximate the original from manufacturer data, but the steering system is simplified and functional only, because details of the military modules are not publicly available.

nodes.label: MTV/LMTV truck models
nodes.rationale: Derived from the public M1078-series LMTV operator's instruction manual (TM-9-2320-365-10).

nodes.label: Polaris MRZR ATV model
nodes.rationale: Based in part on SEA Ltd. VIMF kinematics-and-compliance measurements and dynamic handling/stability tests of a 2013 Polaris MRZR. Documented in the README even though no polaris/ file group exists in the vehicle-models CMakeLists, so the model data lives outside this library target.

nodes.label: UAZ 452/469 vehicle models
nodes.rationale: The Chrono UAZ 469 represents the older design with two solid axles, not the currently sold 'Hunter' which has independent front suspension.

nodes.label: Unimog U401 truck model
nodes.rationale: Vintage Boehringer/Daimler-Benz U401; the main data source is enthusiast-community material (1955 Frosch data sheet) and suspension and steering parameters have been estimated.

nodes.label: Synthetic-data fallback policy for vehicle models
nodes.rationale: For vehicle models not listed in the README, 'synthetic data set at reasonable values' are used. The README exists to make the provenance boundary explicit between measured/published parameters and invented ones.

nodes.label: Salaani et al., SAE 2007-01-0818 (NADS 2006 BMW 330i)
nodes.author: Salaani, M.; Schwarz, C.; Heydinger, G.; Grygier, P.

nodes.label: Aardema, HMMWV rear ball joint failure analysis (TACOM TR 13337)
nodes.author: James Aardema

nodes.label: Wallin et al., comparative study of joint formulations for tracked vehicles
nodes.author: M. Wallin; A.K. Aboubakr; P. Jayakumar; M.D. Letherwood; D.J. Gorsich; A. Hamed; A.A. Shabana

nodes.label: SEA Ltd. Polaris MRZR VIMF and handling test reports (2016)
nodes.author: SEA, Ltd. Vehicle Dynamics Division

nodes.label: Chrono_multicore library target
nodes.rationale: Self-disables without OpenMP or Thrust. Configures Thrust with both THRUST_DEVICE_SYSTEM and THRUST_HOST_SYSTEM set to OMP (unlike the FSI SPH module, which targets CUDA/HIP), and defines EIGEN_DONT_PARALLELIZE to stop Eigen from spawning nested OpenMP threads inside Chrono's own parallel regions.

nodes.label: Multicore iterative solver family (APGD, BB, MINRES, Jacobi, CG, GS, SPGQP)
nodes.rationale: All variants sit behind ChSolverMulticore / ChIterativeSolverMulticore and share the ChDataManager state and the ChSchurProduct operator, so alternative solvers are interchangeable without touching the physics system.

nodes.label: Chrono_mumps library target
nodes.rationale: Requires a Fortran compiler (checked with check_language before enable_language) because MUMPS is Fortran; the module force-disables itself rather than erroring when either the compiler or the MUMPS package is missing. A TODO notes the Windows DLL install cannot work because MUMPS::MUMPS is an umbrella target.

nodes.label: Chrono_pardisomkl library target
nodes.rationale: Wraps Intel oneMKL PARDISO behind ChSolverPardisoMKL; the MKL_ARCH/LINK/THREADING/INTERFACE/MPI cache variables are pre-seeded and marked advanced so users get working defaults (intel64, dynamic, intel_thread, lp64) without reading the oneMKL CMake docs. Also defines EIGEN_USE_MKL_ALL so Eigen routes through MKL.

nodes.label: Chrono_parsers library target
nodes.rationale: Acts as the fan-in point of the build graph: it optionally links PardisoMKL, MUMPS, FSI, FSI-SPH, FSI-TDPF, vehicle and VSG so that a single YAML/URDF/Adams/OpenSim entry point can instantiate models from any enabled module. Feature availability is published to consumers through the generated ChConfigParsers.h (CHRONO_HAS_URDF / PYTHON / ROS).

nodes.label: Optional URDF parser support (CH_USE_URDF)
nodes.rationale: Enabled only when urdfdom plus all of urdfdom_headers, console_bridge and tinyxml2 are found; the flag is exported to PARENT_SCOPE because other modules (robot models, ROS) gate their own sources on it.

nodes.label: Conditional YAML parser file set
nodes.rationale: ChParserYAML/ChParserMbsYAML are the base; FSI, SPH, TDPF and vehicle YAML parsers are appended only when the corresponding modules are enabled, so one parser library grows to cover whatever the build contains instead of forcing a hard module dependency.

nodes.label: run_chrono YAML-driven executable
nodes.rationale: Builds its link list (LIBS) conditionally from every enabled module so a single generic driver binary can run any YAML-specified simulation.

nodes.label: Chrono_peridynamics library target
nodes.rationale: Force-disables itself when CH_ENABLE_MODULE_FEA is off. Note a latent defect: the header install rule references ${Chrono_PardisoMKL_HEADERS} (an undefined variable in this scope, copy-pasted from the PardisoMKL module) instead of ${Chrono_PERIDYNAMICS_HEADERS}, so no headers are installed by that rule. It also lacks the Chrono::peridynamics ALIAS and DEBUG_POSTFIX that every sibling module sets.

nodes.label: Chrono_postprocess library target
nodes.rationale: POV-Ray and Blender exporters are always built; the ChGnuPlot header is added only when a gnuplot executable is found, and CHRONO_HAS_GNUPLOT is pushed to PARENT_SCOPE for the top-level config header.

nodes.label: Chrono_precice library target
nodes.rationale: Adapter layer over preCICE 3.0 for partitioned co-simulation. Only the MBS and SPH adapters are active; the CFD, TDPF and vehicle adapter sources are present but commented out, indicating staged rollout of the adapter family.

nodes.label: run_chrono_adapter executable
nodes.rationale: Same conditional-LIBS driver pattern as run_chrono, but linking Chrono_precice as well; built only when both the parsers module and YAML support are enabled.

nodes.label: chrono_ros_core Static Library
nodes.rationale: Internal STATIC library holding protocol, CDR codec, schema, message codec and shared-memory transport; depends on neither Chrono nor ROS, which is what makes both sides linkable without pulling in the other. Links rt on older glibc for shm_open, plus Threads.

nodes.label: Chrono_ros Simulation-Side Library
nodes.rationale: SHARED public API (manager, bridge, handlers) that links Chrono and chrono_ros_core and contains zero ROS symbols. Handler groups are compiled conditionally: sensor handlers under CH_ENABLE_MODULE_SENSOR (camera/lidar only with OptiX, since their headers pull in optix.h), vehicle handlers under CH_ENABLE_MODULE_VEHICLE, Viper handlers under CH_ENABLE_MODULE_ROBOT_MODELS. Chrono_sensor is linked PUBLIC because handler public headers include chrono_sensor headers, and that is safe precisely because Chrono_sensor is itself ROS-free.

nodes.label: chrono_ros_node Bridge Subprocess
nodes.rationale: Generic rclcpp node linking ROS plus chrono_ros_core and containing zero Chrono symbols. Installed to lib/ on Unix (internal helper, keeps bin/ clean and simplifies RPATH) but to bin/ on Windows for DLL PATH resolution. Message-type packages are not build dependencies: their typesupport is loaded at runtime by name.

nodes.label: Schema-Driven Three-Target ROS Architecture
nodes.rationale: The module is split so that the simulation process never links ROS and the ROS process never links Chrono, with a dependency-free core library carrying the wire protocol between them over shared memory. This is what allows message packages to be resolved at runtime and lets the core be unit-tested with neither ROS nor Chrono installed.

nodes.label: chrono_ros Dev-Time Test Harness
nodes.rationale: Fast inner-loop suites over the dependency-free core plus a stub-header syntax check of the simulation-side API; run under strict warnings with ASan/UBSan. Requires neither ROS nor a Chrono installation - that is the point, since protocol, CDR codec, schema machinery and shm transport are verifiable in isolation. To be registered with Chrono's CTest harness once the module CMake stabilizes.

nodes.label: test_cdr.cpp
nodes.rationale: Covers wire-format golden bytes (alignment, encapsulation, strings), scalar round trips and malformed-input rejection.

nodes.label: test_message.cpp
nodes.rationale: Schema-driven serialization: golden bytes plus Image/PointCloud2/JointState-shaped round trips, defaults and error messages.

nodes.label: test_transport.cpp
nodes.rationale: SPSC ring wraparound, atomic frames and threaded stress; shm channel round trips, capacity diagnostics and control payload codecs.

nodes.label: VALIDATE_TYPE Handshake
nodes.rationale: The authoritative cross-check of the CDR codec against the real rmw, run automatically at every Initialize(); it covers what the dependency-free dev tests structurally cannot (node/ sources, introspection walker, generic pub/sub, end-to-end bridge behavior).

nodes.label: Chrono_sensor_ptx OBJECT Target
nodes.rationale: Separate object library for the OptiX ray-tracing device sources so they are compiled to PTX apart from the host library.

nodes.label: Per-Feature GPU Requirement Declaration
nodes.rationale: GPU requirements are declared per feature, not per module: Chrono::Sensor itself needs no GPU backend because its default renderer is vendor-neutral Vulkan RT, and only the optional OptiX renderer is CUDA-and-NVIDIA-only. Attaching 'requires CUDA' to the module would wrongly disable the whole module on AMD hardware that can run most of it.

nodes.label: Vulkan RT Renderer Backend
nodes.rationale: Default renderer, ON by default and vendor-neutral. The GPU path needs glslangValidator to compile shaders and fails configuration loudly if it is missing, so a CPU-only build must be requested explicitly via CH_USE_SENSOR_VULKAN_RT_GPU=OFF rather than happening silently.

nodes.label: Legacy OptiX Renderer Backend
nodes.rationale: OFF by default and described as legacy; gates the camera and lidar sensor headers (which include optix.h) and therefore also gates the corresponding Chrono::ROS handlers and their installation.

nodes.label: chrono_csharp_wrapper.dll Bundling
nodes.rationale: Optional ready-to-run packaging that gathers every SWIG-generated .cs file into a single managed assembly for downstream consumers; off by default.

nodes.label: SWIG Dependency Tracking (C#)
nodes.rationale: Identical rationale to the Python bindings: swig_add_library() otherwise tracks only the top-level .i file and the IMPLICIT_DEPENDS fallback is Makefile-only, so Visual Studio or Ninja silently miss edits to included interface files.

nodes.label: SWIG Dependency Tracking (Python)
nodes.rationale: SWIG_USE_SWIG_DEPENDENCIES is set so SWIG reports the %include'd interface files and parsed C++ headers as dependencies. By default swig_add_library() tracks only the top-level .i file, and UseSWIG's IMPLICIT_DEPENDS fallback works only with Makefile generators, so under Visual Studio or Ninja an edit to an included interface file was silently ignored until the wrapper output was deleted by hand. Requires CMake 3.20+.

nodes.label: Argout View Arrays zero-copy NumPy wrapping
cudaMemcpy vs optix::map buffer copy trade-off
SCM GPU Ray-Casting Backend
nodes.rationale: Ships ON so hardware decides rather than a flag - an off-by-default accelerator is one most users never turn on; when the toolchain is absent it resolves to NONE and the CPU path runs, which is what a GPU-less machine would do anyway. The requirement is declared for the feature, not for Chrono::Vehicle, and is REQUIRES HIP because the kernels are HIP with no CUDA variant. Both HIP platforms are accepted since nothing here uses the ROCm-only hipCUB/rocPRIM/rocThrust that restrict Chrono::DEM and Chrono::FSI::SPH to amd. Unavailability is reported as IMPLIED and without OPTION, so an absent HIP toolchain is an ordinary fact about the machine rather than a warning, and the cache option is not force-disabled behind the user's back.

nodes.label: Chrono_vehicle_cosim Library Target
nodes.rationale: Node-based co-simulation framework (MBS node, tire nodes, terrain nodes, DBP rig) whose node set expands with whichever Chrono modules are enabled.

nodes.label: Co-simulation Terrain Node Variants
nodes.rationale: Rigid and SCM terrain nodes are always built; GranularOMP is added with Chrono::Multicore, GranularSPH with Chrono::FSI::SPH and GranularDEM with Chrono::DEM, so each granular terrain implementation follows its own solver module.

nodes.label: MPI Requirement for Co-simulation
nodes.rationale: The co-simulation library is a distributed multi-process design, so it links MPI::MPI_CXX PUBLIC and disables itself with a warning when MPI is not found.

nodes.label: Chrono::Vehicle FMI Support
nodes.rationale: Depends on both Chrono::Vehicle and Chrono::FMI; generates ChConfigVehicleFMI.h carrying a common output directory for all vehicle FMUs, and builds co-simulation and model-exchange FMUs only when FMU export is enabled.

nodes.label: FMU_PathFollower Driver
nodes.rationale: Combines a path-follower lateral controller with a cruise-control longitudinal controller in one FMU so the driver can be swapped out of the vehicle simulation as an independent co-simulation participant.

nodes.label: FMU_Powertrain
nodes.rationale: Encapsulates engine plus transmission models specified through JSON files, so powertrain variants can be exchanged without recompiling the FMU.

nodes.label: FMU_WheeledVehicle
nodes.rationale: Vehicle model with neither powertrain nor tires, so both are supplied by separate FMUs across the co-simulation interface.

nodes.label: FMU_WheeledVehiclePtrain
nodes.rationale: Coarser-grained variant bundling the powertrain inside the vehicle FMU, trading co-simulation modularity for fewer coupling interfaces and fewer stability-critical exchange variables.

nodes.label: FMU_ForceElementTire
nodes.rationale: Wraps a Chrono::Vehicle handling (force-element) tire model configured from JSON, the counterpart FMU consumed by the tire-less vehicle FMUs.

nodes.label: FMU2cs_PathFollowerDriver Target
nodes.rationale: Links Chrono_irrlicht when the Irrlicht module is enabled so the driver FMU can render its own path-following debug view; on Windows the Irrlicht DLL is packaged into the FMU via COMPONENT_DLL_DEPENDENCIES.

nodes.label: FMU2me_PathFollowerDriver Target
nodes.rationale: Model-exchange (FMU_ME ON) counterpart of the co-simulation path-follower driver: same sources and same data/vehicle/fmi/path_follower resources, but the importer owns the integrator instead of the FMU. Notably it does not set FMU_TESTING, unlike the co-simulation FMUs.

nodes.label: Chrono::Cascade Demo Programs
nodes.rationale: demo_CAS_stepfile, demo_CAS_robot and demo_CAS_profile all require run-time visualization, so the whole directory returns early unless Irrlicht or VSG is enabled; demo_CAS_converter is Irrlicht-only. OCCT portability defines (WNT on Windows, HAVE_IOSTREAM/HAVE_LIMITS_H on Unix) are applied to Chrono_cascade from inside the demo loop.

nodes.label: Chrono Core Demo Programs
nodes.rationale: Non-visual demos (coords, linalg, matrix_ref, math, archive, buildsystem, powertrain, functions, solver, EulerAngles, filesystem) linked against Chrono_core, optionally augmented with Chrono_pardisomkl and Chrono_mumps direct solvers.

nodes.label: Socket Co-Simulation Demo Programs
nodes.rationale: demo_COSIM_socket, demo_COSIM_data_exchange and demo_COSIM_hydraulics exercise TCP socket co-simulation from Chrono_core only; the directory returns early under EMSCRIPTEN because raw sockets are unavailable in the WebAssembly target.

nodes.label: CHRONO_CSHARP_USING_WRAPPER mode switch
nodes.rationale: Two build modes for C# demos. When CH_USE_CSHARP_WRAPPER is ON the demos reference the prebuilt managed chrono_csharp_wrapper.dll so each executable stays tiny; otherwise every demo falls back to embedding all generated SWIG .cs sources directly (the original approach), which keeps demos standalone-compilable but duplicates the wrapper code into each exe. The wrapper path additionally requires CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY to be set (FATAL_ERROR otherwise) because the DLL reference path is computed from it.

nodes.label: chrono_csharp per-module generated source directories
nodes.rationale: SWIG output is laid out as ${PROJECT_BINARY_DIR}/../chrono_csharp/<module> for core, irrlicht, vsg, postprocess, vehicle, sensor and robot. Because SWIG emits overlapping helper .cs files per module, CollectCSharpFiles de-duplicates each later module against everything already collected before appending, so the same type is never compiled twice into one demo.

nodes.label: Chrono C# SWIG bindings
nodes.rationale: Only a subset of Chrono is SWIG-wrapped for C#: core (explicitly without FEA support), Chrono::Irrlicht, Chrono::VSG and Chrono::Vehicle. Generated scripts and libraries are intended either for external C# programs or for embedding into a Unity project, which is why the output is plain .cs files plus native libraries rather than a NuGet-style package.

nodes.label: C# MBS demo programs (ballSMC, earthquake, link_bushing)
nodes.rationale: Gated on Irrlicht OR VSG being enabled; the visualization backend is selected at C# compile time via /define:CHRONO_IRRLICHT and /define:CHRONO_VSG preprocessor symbols rather than by separate source files.

nodes.label: C# sensor demo programs (demo_CS_SEN_camera)
nodes.rationale: Sensor C# demos are only built when CH_USE_SENSOR_OPTIX is on, because the wrapped sensor pipeline needs the OptiX ray-tracing backend; demo_SEN_Gator remains commented out even under the Irrlicht+Vehicle+VehicleModels guard.

nodes.label: C# vehicle demo programs (Kraz, HMMWV, UAZBUS, Gator, CRGTerrain)
nodes.rationale: Nearly all C# vehicle demos require VSG (not Irrlicht) for run-time visualization; only demo_CS_VEH_paths builds on postprocess alone. Kraz_ClosedLoop additionally needs postprocess and CRGTerrain_VSG needs OpenCRG.

nodes.label: OpenCRG dynamic-object C# reference workaround
nodes.rationale: CRGTerrain demos use C# dynamic objects, which require the Microsoft.CSharp assembly reference on Windows/MSVC. On Unix the build instead requires the Mono package, and the comment marks that path as currently untested. This identical block is duplicated verbatim in the vehicle, sensor and ros C# demo CMakeLists.

nodes.label: DEM demo programs (ballCosim, movingBoundary, fixedTerrain, mixer, repose)
DEMO_FMU_MAIN_DIR (shared FMU output directory)
nodes.rationale: One common output directory (${CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY}/demoFMU) is set once at the FMI demo root and consumed by every FMU subdirectory as COMPONENT_MAIN_DIR and by every driver as a compile definition, so importers can locate exported FMUs at run time without hard-coded paths.

nodes.label: Chrono::FMI examples
nodes.rationale: The example set is organized along two orthogonal axes: FMI kind (co-simulation vs model exchange) and FMI version (2.0 vs 3.0), so that each Chrono model (hydraulic actuator, double-pendulum crane, Van der Pol oscillator) demonstrates both export and import through fmu-forge.

nodes.label: fmusim FMU validation tool
nodes.rationale: Exported FMUs are automatically round-tripped through the Reference-FMUs fmusim validator during the build when CH_ENABLE_FMU_TESTING is ON, so a malformed modelDescription.xml or missing binary is caught at export time rather than in a downstream importer.

nodes.label: Simulink FMU import / co-simulation validation
nodes.rationale: The FMI 2.0 CS crane and actuator FMUs were imported into Simulink and co-simulated there as third-party proof that the exported FMUs are standard-conformant, not just self-consistent with Chrono's own importer.

nodes.label: demo_FMI2_hydraulic_crane_cosim (FMI 2.0 co-simulation driver)
nodes.rationale: The driver learns about the FMUs it will load entirely through compile definitions (model identifier, directory, filename, runtime output directory) exported by the FMU subdirectories via PARENT_SCOPE, plus FMI2_PLATFORM and SHARED_LIBRARY_SUFFIX so it can assemble the platform-specific binary path inside the unzipped FMU.

nodes.label: FMU2cs_actuator (hydraulic actuator, FMI 2.0 co-simulation FMU)
nodes.rationale: Built by declaring the local fmu-forge fmi2 tree as a FetchContent source dir rather than downloading it, so the FMU packaging target is generated in-tree; the resulting identifier/paths are exported to PARENT_SCOPE for the driver to consume.

nodes.label: FMU2cs_crane (double-pendulum crane, FMI 2.0 co-simulation FMU)
nodes.rationale: Unlike the actuator FMU, the crane FMU can embed Irrlicht visualization; when Irrlicht is enabled on Windows the Irrlicht DLL is added to COMPONENT_DLL_DEPENDENCIES so it is packaged inside the .fmu binaries folder and the FMU stays self-contained for an external importer.

nodes.label: demo_FMI_VdP_modex (Van der Pol model-exchange driver)
nodes.rationale: A single driver imports both the FMI 2.0 and the FMI 3.0 VdP FMU (VDP_FMU2_FILENAME and VDP_FMU3_FILENAME are both compiled in), demonstrating that Chrono_fmi abstracts over the two FMI versions on the import side.

nodes.label: demo_FMI_hydraulic_crane_modex (actuator model-exchange driver)
nodes.rationale: Only the FMI 2.0 actuator FMU is wired in; the ACTUATOR_FMU3_FILENAME compile definition is present but commented out because no fmu3 model-exchange actuator subdirectory exists.

FSI backend subdirectory dispatch (SPH / TDPF)
nodes.rationale: FSI demos are partitioned by fluid solver backend (SPH vs TDPF), each guarded by its own CH_ENABLE_MODULE_FSI_* flag, so enabling one solver does not pull in demos that link the other solver's library.

nodes.label: FSI-SPH demo programs (DamBreak, WaveTank, flexible-body suite)
nodes.rationale: The flexible-body FSI demos (Flexible_Plate, Flexible_Cable, Flexible_Toroidal_Tire, FEAdirections) are gated on FEA *and* PARDISO_MKL together, because deformable solids coupled to SPH need a direct sparse solver for the structural side; demo_FSI-SPH_BCE is VSG-only since it exists to visualize boundary-condition-enforcing marker layouts.

FMU_FORGE_DIR Include Path Override
nodes.rationale: The FMI tests include fmu-forge headers directly rather than through a Chrono target, so the fmu-forge top-level directory must be added to each test's include path. The variable FMU_FORGE_DIR is used instead of a hard-coded in-tree submodule path so that a user override of the fmu-forge location is honored.

nodes.label: FEA-Gated Modal Test Registration
nodes.rationale: The modal test list starts empty and is populated only when CH_ENABLE_MODULE_FEA is on, because every modal test (eigensolver, curved beam, cache reduced) exercises flexible-body models that only exist with the FEA module built. PardisoMKL is appended to the link libraries only when that module is enabled, so the modal tests can use the direct sparse solver when available without making it a hard dependency.

nodes.label: CTest Working Directory And PYTHONPATH Injection
nodes.rationale: Python tests are run with an explicitly set WORKING_DIRECTORY because the Chrono data directory is reached through a relative path, so the tests only resolve their data when launched from the executable output path (with a Release subfolder on Windows, matching the multi-config generator layout). PYTHONPATH is composed from PYTHONPATH_BUILD plus the inherited environment using a platform-specific separator (';' on Windows, ':' elsewhere), and on Windows the semicolons are escaped because CMake would otherwise treat the joined string as a list and split it into multiple environment entries.
